html:
The Skagit are Lushootseed-speaking Coast Salish peoples of the Skagit River valley in northwestern Washington, from the delta and islands of Skagit Bay up into the North Cascades. The Lower Skagit lived near the coast and the Upper Skagit along the river.

They fished for salmon, hunted, gathered roots and berries and traded across the mountains. In 1855 Skagit leaders signed the Treaty of Point Elliott, but no reservation was set aside for the Upper Skagit, who won federal recognition only in the 1970s. Lower Skagit descendants are now largely part of the Swinomish tribe. Their neighbours include the Sauk-Suiattle, Stillaguamish and Snohomish, all part of the wider Coast Salish world.
